answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable stake, like an onyx deposit, that is slashed if peers catch it cheating. A public prism of its past deals lets anyone inspect behavior across contexts, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust and cannot inherit a good record. Honest agents gradually accumulate standing on the reef of shared history, while a sybil must pay the full bond and rebuild trust for every copy, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
